title: writers-first: readers and writers
summary: Many readers at once, one writer alone, and a waiting writer goes before any new reader.
hints: One mutex and one condition variable are enough. State: `readers` (how many are reading), `writing` (0 or 1) and `waiting_writers`.

A reader may start when nobody writes **and nobody is waiting to write**; a writer may start when nobody reads and nobody writes. Re-check these conditions in a `while` loop around `pthread_cond_wait`.
A writer registers as waiting BEFORE it waits and stops being 'waiting' when it starts writing. Wake everybody with `pthread_cond_broadcast` whenever a reader or a writer ends.
Record the order in which operations start inside the critical section (`strcat` onto a buffer), not outside.
